skill.title: Find an integer root by trial
needs: Test a factor with the Factor Theorem

lines.text: Try small whole numbers. Let $f(x) = x^3 - 3x^2 - 9x + 11$.
So $x = 1$ is a root and $(x - 1)$ is a factor.

steps.title: Write the other factor with an unknown

lines.text: The cubic has the form $(x-1)$ times a quadratic. The constant of the quadratic is $-11$, because $-1 \times -11 = 11$.

steps.title: Compare the coefficients of x squared
Solve the quadratic with the formula

lines.text: $x^2 - 2x - 11 = 0$ does not factorise, so use $x = \frac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a}$ with $a = 1$, $b = -2$, $c = -11$.
The irrational solutions are $1 + 2\sqrt{3}$ and $1 - 2\sqrt{3}$, of the form $a + b\sqrt{c}$ with $a = 1$, $b = \pm 2$, $c = 3$.

skill.example: (x − 2) is a factor of x³ + kx² − 4x + 12 → k = −3

steps.title: Split the middle terms so (x + 4) appears in each group
Write the cubic as the quadratic times a linear factor

lines.text: A quadratic factor of a cubic leaves a linear factor $(x + k)$.

lines.tex: x^3 + kx^2 - px^2 - pkx + x + k &= x^3 - 2x - 3r

lines.text: The right-hand side has no $x^2$ term, so its coefficient is $0$.
